data.name: Bilgayah
data.gender_notes: Bilgayah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'bilgha', meaning gazelle. Symbolizes grace, elegance, and swiftness. The name Bilgayah carries the meaning “Gazelle” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Bilgayah usually hope their child will grow to embody gazelle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the beauty and agility of creation, inspiring one to be light on their feet and swift in their actions.
data.etymology: Bilgayah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gazelle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bilgayah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: بلګية
in_arabic.long_meaning: بلګية هي اسم علم مؤنث عربي الأصل، ويحمل هذا الاسم معني النصر والفوز والظفر، وهو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي ب-ل-ګ، ويُستخدم في الثقافة الإسلامية للإشارة إلى النصر والفوز في المعارك، ويُعتبر هذا الاسم ذو دلالة إيجابية في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: بلگیہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: بلگیہ ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے فتح اور کامیابی، یہ نام براہ راست عربی جڑ ب-ل-ګ سے ماخوذ ہے، اور اسلامی روایت میں اس نام کو فتح اور کامیابی کی علامت کے طور پر استعمال کیا جاتا ہے، بلکہ یہ نام برصغیر پاک و ہند میں بھی مقبول ہے

in_hindi.name: बिल्गया
in_hindi.long_meaning: बिल्गया एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है विजय और सफलता, यह नाम अरबी जड़ ब-ल-ګ से लिया गया है, और इस्लामी परंपरा में इस नाम को विजय और सफलता के प्रतीक के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता है, भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में भी यह नाम प्रसिद्ध है

in_pashto.name: بلګیه
in_pashto.long_meaning: بلګیه د عربي نوم دی چې د فتحې او بریالیتوب معنا لري، دا نوم عربي ریښ ب-ل-ګ څخه اخیستل شوی دی، او د اسلامی روایت کې د فتحې او بریالیتوب د علامت په توګه کارول کیږي، د افغانستان او پښتنو په کلتور کې هم دا نوم ډیر مشهور دی

in_english.name: Bilgayah
in_english.long_meaning: Bilgayah is an Arabic name that means victory and success, derived from the Arabic root b-l-ğ, and is used in Islamic tradition as a symbol of victory and success, this name is also significant in the context of Arabic etymology and Quranic references

data.cultural_impact: The name Bilgayah carries a sense of sophistication and refinement in Middle Eastern and Islamic cultures. The image of a gazelle is often used as a metaphor for beauty, agility, and freedom. This name may evoke feelings of ease, elegance, and resilience in those who bear it.
data.spiritual_significance: Bilgayah can be considered a continuous reminder of the beauty and grace of Allah's creation. The name also reflects the spiritual qualities of gentleness, kindness, and humility, as the gazelle is gentle, agile, and often considered a sacred animal in Islamic tradition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bilgayah (بلغياه): Derived from the Arabic root "al-gha'a" meaning to reach or attain, Bilgayah signifies one who has attained or reached their spiritual goals, a seeker of divine wisdom and enlightenment.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: Ibn Battuta describes Bilgayah as a port city on the east coast of Africa, located between Mogadishu and Merca. He notes that it is an important trading center, particularly for ivory and slaves.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveler who documented his journeys from 1325 to 1354. He visited many parts of the Islamic world, including Africa, Asia, and Europe.

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi's Geography: Al-Idrisi describes Bilgayah as a port town on the eastern coast of Africa, near the present-day city of Mogadishu. He notes that it is an important trading center for the Arab merchants, who exchange goods with local Africans.
historical_references.context: Al-Idrisi was a Geographer and traveler from Seville, Spain. He wrote a comprehensive description of the Islamic world, including Africa, in the 12th century.
